arxiv-2210-12042.title: Neural Network-Based Multi-Target Detection within Correlated Heavy-Tailed Clutter
arxiv-2210-12042.creator: S. Feintuch, H. Permuter, Senior Member, IEEE , I. Bilik, Senior Member, IEEE , and J. Tabrikian, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2210-12042.description: Abstract This work addresses the problem of range-Doppler multiple target detection in a radar system in the presence of slow-time correlated and heavy-tailed distributed clutter. Conventional target detection algorithms assume Gaussian-distributed clutter, but their performance is significantly degraded in the presence of correlated heavy-tailed distributed clutter. Derivation of optimal detection algorithms with heavy-tailed distributed clutter is analytically intractable.

arxiv-2409-04517.title: Higher-derivative corrections to the Kerr quasinormal mode spectrum
arxiv-2409-04517.creator: Pablo A. Cano, Lodovico Capuano, Nicola Franchini, Simon Maenaut, Sebastian H. Völkel
arxiv-2409-04517.description: Abstract We provide the most complete analysis so far of quasinormal modes of rotating black holes in a general higher-derivative extension of Einstein’s theory. By finding the corrections to the Teukolsky equation and expressing them in a simple form, we are able to apply a generalized continued fraction method that allows us to find the quasinormal mode frequencies including overtones.

arxiv-2501-09164.title: The Veln(ia)s is in the Details: Evaluating LLM Judgment on Latvian and Lithuanian Short Answer Matching
arxiv-2501-09164.creator: Yevhen Kostiuk, Oxana VitmanUniversity of Bremen, Łukasz GagałaGeorg-AugustUniversität Göttingen, Artur KiulianOpenBabylon
arxiv-2501-09164.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yevhen Kostiuk, Oxana VitmanUniversity of Bremen, Łukasz GagałaGeorg-AugustUniversität Göttingen, Artur KiulianOpenBabylon. In this work, we address the challenge of evaluating large language models (LLMs) on the short answer matching task for Latvian and Lithuanian languages. We introduce novel datasets consisting of 502 Latvian and 690 Lithuanian question-answer pairs. For each question-answer pair, we generated matched and non-matched answers using a set of alteration rules specifically designed to introduce small but meaningful changes in the text.

arxiv-2506-20760.title: Constant-Factor Improvements in Quantum Algorithms for Linear Differential Equations
arxiv-2506-20760.creator: Matthew Pocrnic, Peter D. Johnson, Amara Katabarwa, Nathan Wiebe
arxiv-2506-20760.description: Abstract Finding the solution to linear ordinary differential equations of the form ∂ t u ⁡ ( t ) = − A ⁡ ( t ) ​ u ​ ( t ) \partial_{t}u(t)=-A(t)u(t) has been a promising theoretical avenue for asymptotic quantum speedups.

arxiv-2601-13713.title: SWE-Tester: Training Open-Source LLMs for Issue Reproduction in Real-World Repositories
arxiv-2601-13713.creator: Aditya Bharat Soni, Rajat Ghosh, Vaishnavi Bhargava, Valerie Chen, Debojyoti Dutta
arxiv-2601-13713.description: Abstract Software testing is crucial for ensuring the correctness and reliability of software systems. Automated generation of issue reproduction tests from natural language issue descriptions enhances developer productivity by simplifying root cause analysis, promotes test-driven development – “test first, write code later”, and can be used for improving the effectiveness of automated issue resolution systems like coding agents.

pmc-10495639.title: Calculating RNA degradation rates using large-scale normalization in mouse embryonic stem cells
pmc-10495639.creator: Juliane Oliveira Viegas, Lior Fishman, Eran Meshorer, Michal Rabani
pmc-10495639.description: SummaryData normalization is critical to the process of estimating RNA degradation by analyzing RNA levels when transcription is blocked. Here, we present a protocol for measuring mRNA degradation rates, optimized for mouse embryonic stem cells, using α-amanitin inhibitor. We describe steps for a time course α-amanitin treatment, RNA-seq, and alignment; we then detail procedures for analyzing data and sequence enrichment.

pmc-11714140.title: Impact of beta‐amyloid oligomers on in vivo brain glucose metabolism
pmc-11714140.creator: Andreia Silva da Rocha, Igor C. Fontana, Guilherme G. Schu Peixoto, Amanda S Souza, Gianina Teribele Venturin, Samuel Greggio, Leticia Forny‐Germano, Mychael V Lourenco, Pedro Rosa‐Neto, Diogo O. Souza, Jaderson Costa da Costa, Sergio T Ferreira, Eduardo R. Zimmer
pmc-11714140.description: BackgroundThe deposition of β‐amyloid (Aβ) plaques is a classical neuropathological feature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Currently, it is believed that intermediate products of the Aβ fibrillogenesis process, like the β‐amyloid oligomers (AβOs), are the most toxic forms, and are involved in neurodegenerative processes in AD.

pmc-12402237.description: Lung cancer is the most common cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, and early detection is extremely important for improving survival. According to the National Institute of Health Sciences, lung cancer has the highest rate of cancer mortality, according to the National Institute of Health Sciences.

pmc-12613787.title: Exploring the knowledge, attitudes, and potential role of oral health practitioners in FASD screening in South Africa
pmc-12613787.creator: Imaan Amina Roomaney, Clement Nyirenda, Manogari Chetty
pmc-12613787.description: BackgroundSouth Africa has the highest global burden of foetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD), yet awareness and prioritisation among healthcare professionals remain limited. Oral health practitioners (OHPs) are well-positioned to support FASD screening due to their community presence and craniofacial expertise. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and readiness of South African OHPs to engage in FASD screening.

pmc-12986739.title: AWG-Based Spectral Multiplexing for Unambiguous Range-Extended FMCW LiDAR
pmc-12986739.creator: Sangwon Park, Sang Min Park, Seongmun Jeong, Gyeongmin Kweon, Chang-Seok Kim, Hwidon Lee
pmc-12986739.description: Frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) based on coherent ranging is a technology capable of high-resolution distance measurement while remaining robust against ambient light interference. However, extending the measurable range remains challenging due to (i) the coherence length limitation of the laser and (ii) distance ambiguity caused by frequency ambiguity in coherent detection.

pmc-13147610.title: Gait analysis reveals new outcome measures for monitoring disease progression in individuals with late-onset Pompe disease
pmc-13147610.creator: Mireia Claramunt-Molet, Jordi Pegueroles, Ariadna Pi-Cervera, Mari Rico, Sebastian Idelsohn-Zielonka, Cristina Domínguez-González, Manuela Corti, Virgilia Antón, Stephanie M Salabarria, Karen Wong, Meredith K James, Barry J Byrne, Jordi Díaz-Manera
pmc-13147610.description: BackgroundLate-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) presents with progressive muscle weakness, often leading to functional impairment that is challenging to monitor with conventional assessments. This study aims to develop and validate novel gait-based outcome measures for monitoring disease progression in individuals with LOPD.

pmc-13604548.title: Longitudinal Sodium Dynamics After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Single-Center Cohort Study with a Contemporary Literature Review
pmc-13604548.creator: Adrianna Lebiedzińska, Jarosław Kędziora, Jowita Woźniak, Katarzyna Smarzewska, Waldemar Goździk, Małgorzata Burzyńska
pmc-13604548.description: Background and Objectives: Disorders of sodium homeostasis are common after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), but the prognostic value of longitudinal sodium dynamics remains unclear. We evaluated whether dynamic sodium parameters provide prognostic information beyond admission sodium concentration. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 232 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed aSAH admitted between January 2014 and December 2025.
